newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Little rain seen in Philippines thanks to El Nino.
newsitem.headline: Little rain seen in Philippines thanks to El Nino.

text.p: The Philippine weather bureau said on Tuesday it expected below-average rainfall over the next two months due to the El Nino phenomenon.

"The warm episode in the central and eastern tropical Pacific (has been) getting stronger in the past few months and it increases the threat (of affecting) the country's rainfall condition," bureau director Leoncio Amadore said.

The Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) said most parts of the country experienced sparse rains between April and July this year due to fewer-than-usual cyclones.
The Philippines was supposed to be at the height of its rainy season now, which normally starts April and ends in September.

"The remaining months of the southwest monsoon season (August to September) will be affected that would likely result (in) below normal rainfall conditions in most parts of the country especially the western sections," Amadore said in his latest advisory on the El Nino.
El Nino is caused by the warming of water in the western Pacific ocean, which creates disparate weather phenomena such as drought in some areas and heavier-than- normal rainfall in others.
"Concerned government agencies are advised to take appropriate measures to mitigate the potential adverse impact of the impending situation," he added.
